title: Comparison of Mapping Approaches on the Held-Out Partition
note: Waste class, 216 spatially clean held-out tiles, label 99 excluded, mean of three seeds with the standard deviation in parentheses, argmax decision rule. FPR is the false-positive rate. Gap is the achieved FPR divided by the FPR that precision 0.5 would require at the landscape prevalence of 0.045%; a directly usable map would have a gap of 1.0. Models are selected on the validation split by the one-standard-error rule (highest validation F1, then lowest deployability gap among configurations within one standard error of it) and only then evaluated on the held-out partition. The rule selects DINOv3 ViT-L (SAT-493M). Val. F1 is shown so that the selection can be checked; it is not a performance claim.

title: Pretrained and Foundation-Model Backbones, Frozen Versus Fine-Tuned
note: Ordered by validation F1, which is the quantity selection is made on. All ten configurations transferred 100% of their checkpoint tensors, verified against a freshly initialised model of the same specification (preflight_report.json). PR-AUC is threshold independent. Min. is training minutes per seed on one GPU. Other columns as in Table I.

title: Waste-Class F1 by Annotation Budget and Pretraining Corpus
note: Held-out F1, mean of three seeds, argmax rule. n is the number of annotated training tiles. The same tile subset is drawn for every seed at a given budget, so the spread across seeds reflects training stochasticity only and not the variance of the subset itself; the budget effect is therefore reported as an order of magnitude and not as a point estimate. Rows ordered by F1 at the smallest budget.

title: Effect of the Complementary Not-Waste Loss Weight
note: Raising the weight suppresses false positives but removes recall with them. Implied precision is the Bayes projection of the measured recall and FPR to the landscape prevalence of 0.045%. n.d. means the gap is not determined: at least one seed returned zero recall, so the required FPR is zero and the ratio is undefined. Scratch architecture throughout.

title: Attainable Operating Set: the Recall-Gap Pareto Frontier
note: A configuration is on the frontier when no other configuration attains both a higher recall and a lower gap, so this is the complete set of non-dominated operating points over all 54 configurations. Trading recall for precision moves along the frontier; it does not leave it. The gap exceeds 11 at every attainable point, including those that discard more than nine tenths of the waste.

title: Every Reported Configuration, Ranked by Deployability Gap
note: No configuration approaches a gap of 1.0. Configurations marked 'no' under usable recall return less than 35% of the waste and reach a low gap only by declining to detect; they are retained for completeness and excluded from the ranges quoted in the text.

title: GeoBIA Model Development, Evaluated at Segment Level
note: Segment-level accuracy measures how well segments are labelled once they exist. It is not comparable with the pixel-level results in Tables I and III to XI, which measure how well the resulting map delineates waste on the ground, and it is reported only to document how the GeoBIA classifier was chosen. The pixel-level GeoBIA result is in Table I.

title: Spatial Distribution of False Positives on the Held-Out Partition
note: Of the 216 spatially clean held-out tiles, 80 contain at least one waste pixel. A false positive inside such a tile is a delineation error; one in a tile with no waste is a false detection in unfamiliar background. Counts are means over seeds. Reported for every configuration that stored per-tile confusion counts; the backbone comparison of Table IV did not store them, so the selected model is not listed and the pattern should be read as a property of this imagery rather than of one architecture.

title: Land Cover Confused With Waste on the Held-Out Partition
note: All figures are percentages, computed on the 216 spatially clean held-out tiles with label 99 excluded, under the argmax rule. Share of scene is the fraction of assessed pixels belonging to the class. Commission rate is the fraction of that class predicted waste, and is independent of how much of the class the scene contains. Share of errors is the fraction of all false-positive pixels whose true class is the one named. Means over 4 configurations, each itself a mean over three seeds, with the range across configurations. For reference, recall on the waste class itself averages 68.0%. Rows ordered by commission rate.

title: Waste-Class F1 Under Simulated Loss of Spatial Resolution
note: Held-out imagery reduced by area averaging and restored to the 256 x 256 evaluation grid by bilinear interpolation, so every value is measured against the same reference mask. The first column is the native ground sample distance of 3.81 cm. Mean of 3 seeds. Rows ordered by the fraction of accuracy retained at twice the pixel size. Masks are never perturbed.

title: Waste-Class F1 Under a Change of Scene Brightness
note: Held-out imagery multiplied by a gain and clipped to the 8-bit range, simulating the exposure and illumination differences between flights. x1.00 is the unperturbed image. Mean of 3 seeds. Row order as in Table IX. Worst case retained is the lowest fraction of native-resolution F1 over all gains tested.
